lessons.title: Days of the week
lessons.goal: Name the days and say what day it is.

tip.title: el lunes = on Monday
tip.body: Days are written with a small letter and are masculine. To say "on Monday" just use el: el lunes trabajo (on Monday I work). For "every Monday" use los: los lunes. Lunes to viernes are the same in the plural; only sábados and domingos add -s.

phrases.t: Los domingos como con mi familia.
phrases.n: On Sundays I have lunch with my family.

lines.name: Andrés
lines.n: What day is it today?
Today is Friday.

lines.name: Andrés
lines.n: Great! What are you doing at the weekend?

lines.t: El sábado estudio español y el domingo descanso.
lines.n: On Saturday I study Spanish and on Sunday I rest.

prompts.n: Ask what day it is today.

tip.title: Es la una, son las dos
tip.body: Hours are feminine because they mean las horas: es la una (one o'clock, singular), but son las dos, son las tres… Add minutes with y (past) and menos (to): y cuarto (quarter past), y media (half past), menos cuarto (quarter to). So son las cinco menos cuarto is 4:45. Spain usually says ¿Qué hora es?; in Latin America you'll also hear ¿Qué horas son?.

lines.n: Excuse me, what time is it?

lines.name: Señora
lines.n: It's half past four.
Oh, it's late! Thank you very much.

lines.name: Señora
lines.n: You're welcome. All the best!

prompts.n: Politely ask a stranger what time it is.

lessons.title: Finding a time
lessons.goal: Ask when someone is free and suggest a day and time.

tip.title: ¿Te viene bien…?
tip.body: ¿Te viene bien el martes? (Does Tuesday suit you?) is an easy way to suggest a day. In Spain friends say ¿Quedamos el martes? (Shall we meet on Tuesday?); quedar is less common in Latin America, where ¿Nos vemos el martes? is the usual choice. Nos vemos works everywhere.

phrases.t: Tengo una cita con el médico.

lines.name: Sara
lines.n: Shall we have a coffee today?

lines.t: Hoy no puedo. Tengo una cita con el médico.
lines.n: I can't today. I have a doctor's appointment.

lines.name: Sara
lines.n: And tomorrow? Does that suit you?

lines.t: Sí, mañana sí puedo. ¿A qué hora?
lines.n: Yes, tomorrow I can. At what time?

lines.name: Sara
lines.t: A las seis, en la plaza.
lines.n: At six, in the square.
Perfect. See you tomorrow!

prompts.n: Ask a friend when they're free.

lessons.title: Es la una / a la una
lessons.goal: Tell the time and say when something happens.

tip.title: ser for the time, a for "at"
tip.body: To say what time it is, use ser: es la una, son las ocho. To say when something happens, use a + la/las: a la una (at one), a las ocho (at eight). Ask with ¿A qué hora…?: ¿A qué hora abre el banco? (What time does the bank open?). Add de la mañana, de la tarde or de la noche to make clear which part of the day: a las nueve de la noche (at 9 p.m.).

phrases.t: La clase es a las ocho.

phrases.n: What time does the bank open?

phrases.t: Abre a las nueve de la mañana.
phrases.n: It opens at nine in the morning.

phrases.t: Cenamos a las nueve de la noche.
phrases.n: We have dinner at nine in the evening.

base.t: La clase es a las ocho.

items.t: La clase es a la una.
La clase es a las diez y media.
items.n: The class is at half past ten.

items.t: La clase es a las seis y cuarto.
items.n: The class is at quarter past six.

items.t: La clase es a las nueve menos cuarto.
items.n: The class is at quarter to nine.

items.t: El tren sale a las dos.

prompts.n: Ask what time the shop opens.
t: A qué hora abre la tienda

prompts.n: Say the film is at half past nine.
t: La película es a las nueve y media
La peli es a las nueve y media

lessons.title: A busy week
lessons.goal: Catch days and times in a real conversation.

story.title: Daniela calls Rodrigo
story.intro: Daniela, in Mexico City, wants to go to the cinema with Rodrigo this week, but he is busy.

lines.name: Daniela
lines.n: Hi, Rodrigo! Shall we go to the cinema on Monday?

lines.name: Rodrigo
lines.t: ¿El lunes? Imposible, trabajo hasta las siete y luego tengo clase de inglés.
lines.n: On Monday? Impossible, I work until seven and then I have an English class.

lines.name: Daniela
lines.n: And on Wednesday?

lines.name: Rodrigo
lines.t: El miércoles me viene bien. ¿A qué hora es la película?
lines.n: Wednesday suits me. What time is the film?

lines.name: Daniela
lines.t: Hay una función a las ocho y media.
lines.n: There's a showing at half past eight.

lines.name: Rodrigo
lines.t: Perfecto. Te veo a las ocho y cuarto en la entrada.
lines.n: Perfect. I'll see you at quarter past eight at the entrance.

lines.name: Daniela
lines.n: OK! See you on Wednesday.

questions.q: ¿Hasta qué hora trabaja Rodrigo el lunes?
questions.n: Until what time does Rodrigo work on Monday?
Which day are they going to the cinema?

t: Es a las ocho y media

lessons.title: Booking a haircut
lessons.goal: Make an appointment on the phone.

phrases.n: I'd like to make an appointment.
phrases.note: Using quería ("I wanted") is a softer, polite way to ask.

branch.title: Calling the hair salon
branch.scene: You phone a hair salon in Barcelona to book a haircut this week.
branch.name: Peluquería Nuria

choices.t: Buenos días. Quería pedir una cita, por favor.
choices.n: Good morning. I'd like to make an appointment, please.

repeat.t: Es la peluquería. ¿En qué le puedo ayudar?
repeat.n: This is the hair salon. How can I help you?

day.t: Muy bien. ¿Qué día le viene bien?
day.n: Very good. Which day suits you?

monday.t: Lo siento, los lunes está cerrado. ¿Le viene bien el viernes?
monday.n: Sorry, we're closed on Mondays. Does Friday suit you?

friday.t: El viernes tengo hueco a las diez o a las cinco y media.
friday.n: On Friday I have a slot at ten or at half past five.

choices.t: A las cinco y media, por favor.

name.t: Perfecto. ¿Me dice su nombre, por favor?
name.n: Perfect. Could you tell me your name, please?

done.n: Thanks, Alex. See you on Friday. Bye!
done.outcome: You booked a haircut for Friday.

pizza.n: Pizza? This is a hair salon. Goodbye.
pizza.outcome: Off-topic! Try again and ask for una cita.

t: Quería pedir una cita por favor
A las diez me viene bien

lessons.title: My week
lessons.goal: Talk about your week for 45 seconds.

culture.title: Late dinners and ahorita
culture.body: Spain eats late: lunch is usually around 2 to 3 p.m. and dinner often starts around 9 p.m. or even later, and many restaurants only start serving dinner at around 8:30 or 9. In Mexico you'll hear ahorita all the time; it literally means "right now", but depending on tone and context it can mean "in a moment", "later" or even "maybe never". If you need something soon, ask ¿Ahorita ahorita? or agree on a clear time. Timetables, tickets and opening hours across the Spanish-speaking world often use the 24-hour clock (las 21:00), but in speech people usually say las nueve de la noche.

phrases.n: In Spain people have dinner late.

phrases.note: ahorita can mean now, soon or later!

phrases.t: Los fines de semana no trabajo.
phrases.n: I don't work at the weekend.

free.n: Describe your week: what you do on which days and at what time.
free.hint: El lunes trabajo … · Los martes estudio español … · Me levanto a las siete · Ceno a las ocho · El fin de semana …
free.model: El lunes trabajo de nueve a cinco. Los martes estudio español a las siete de la tarde. El viernes ceno con mis amigos a las nueve. El fin de semana no trabajo y descanso.

prompts.n: Say you don't work at the weekend.
t: Los fines de semana no trabajo
El fin de semana no trabajo
No trabajo el fin de semana
